summary: Verified the refreshing-pill polish on /dashboard. Logged in as admin, auto-accepted disclaimer via /api/disclaimer/accept, then triggered re-analyze on AAPL (which already had a BUY verdict). The refreshing-pill-{ticker} overlay renders correctly: it has the .refreshing-pill class, the refreshingPulse @keyframes animation runs, contains a Loader2 svg animated via 'spin', the text resolves to 'Refreshing…' (uppercased visually by .text-overline siblings but raw textContent is 'Refreshing…'), pointer-events is 'none', overlay is position:absolute inside a position:relative cell, pill geometrically fits inside the verdict-cell bounds on both desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844). No horizontal overflow on mobile. After the 56s analysis completed the pill was removed and the inner wrapper's opacity returned to 1. Zero console errors throughout the full flow.

ui_bugs.issue: Playwright's strict hit-test consistently reports that the inner verdict-cell div (DashboardPage.jsx line 84, the opacity wrapper around SignalBadge) subtree intercepts pointer events at the analyze-{ticker}-button click coordinate, even on 1920px desktop where the two columns should be visually separate. Real mouse clicks currently work (iter 17 passed) but this indicates an invisible bounding-box overlap likely caused by the new `relative` wrapper + internal flow content of SignalBadge/conf text extending beyond its grid cell. Risk: touch targets on narrow viewports, possible flakiness for any automated tests that click the analyze/timeline/view/remove buttons. Reproduced 3 times; required switching to element.click() via page.evaluate() to bypass.

action_items: Investigate why the verdict-cell-{ticker} subtree overlaps the analyze button's hit area geometrically. Likely candidates: SignalBadge has display:inline-block with min-width, or the conf/timeAgo text-overline child is rendering wider than its grid column due to letter-spacing. Consider adding `min-w-0 overflow-hidden` or `pointer-events:none` on the inner dimmed wrapper (the pointer-events trick is safe since there are no interactive children inside it).

(Minor, carry-over from iter 17) Wire the 8s safety-net setTimeout inside analyzeOne to a useEffect cleanup so it is cancelled on unmount; align verdict-revealed setTimeout to the 1600ms keyframe duration.
critical_code_review_comments: DashboardPage.jsx WatchlistRow lines 82-115: the dimmed inner wrapper has no pointer-events:none and no overflow:hidden, so any content that accidentally widens the verdict-cell bounding box bleeds into the sibling action-buttons column's hit area. Adding `pointerEvents: 'none'` to the opacity wrapper fixes hit-testing without changing the visual — users never need to click the verdict text.

The inline style `transition: 'opacity 200ms ease-out'` on the dim wrapper combined with immediate pill render can cause snapshot tests that read computed opacity within the first 200ms of the click to observe an interpolated value (we saw a read of exactly '1' in one snapshot). Mid-transition reads are brittle; consider using a CSS class toggled via className (so tests can assert class presence) rather than inline style opacity.

refreshing-pill uses `items-center justify-start` so when the verdict row's grid col shrinks on very narrow displays, the pill may visually align with the BUY badge rather than the full cell. On 390px viewport this worked fine, but if SignalBadge becomes compact the pill could start at an awkward offset — consider `justify-center` for better visual centering on narrow columns.

success_rate.frontend: Desktop: pill feature PASS (9/10 atomic checks; opacity computed style read as 1 during pill due to CSS 200ms transition timing — mobile snapshot of same flow returned correctly). Mobile 390: PASS (pill within cell, no overflow). Post-analysis cleanup PASS. Console errors: 0. Regression path (fresh-ticker → analyzing-label) was NOT re-verified in the final dispatch-click run due to Loop Prevention on the initial click-intercept issue; Iteration 17 already verified the analyzing-label path end-to-end for NFLX, and the code branch is unchanged, so functionally-equivalent.

context_for_next_testing_agent: If Playwright click on analyze-{ticker}-button fails with 'subtree intercepts pointer events' from the verdict-cell, use `page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector('[data-testid=analyze-AAPL-button]').click())` to dispatch the click via DOM — force=True alone does NOT bypass the interceptor because the button becomes visibly unreachable. Backend disclaimer must be pre-accepted (POST /api/disclaimer/accept) or the Analyze flow silently opens the modal without showing in data-testid during the automated flow.
rca of the issue: The refreshing-pill polish is correctly implemented in CSS (@keyframes refreshingPulse, .refreshing-pill 1.4s infinite in index.css:444-450) and in JSX (WatchlistRow in DashboardPage.jsx:82-115 — verdict-cell wrapper is position:relative, dim wrapper has inline opacity 0.4 when analyzing + latest_analysis exists, pill is absolute inset-0 with pointer-events-none). Observed behaviour matches spec: pill appears on re-analyze, disappears on completion. The only concern is that the new wrapper `className='relative'` introduced a geometric issue where the verdict-cell subtree intercepts the analyze button's hit area in Playwright's elementFromPoint check. Mitigation: add `pointerEvents:'none'` to the dim wrapper inline style, which preserves the visual exactly and unblocks hit-testing for both humans and automation.
